## VERIFIED — all 7 criteria met; the split landed as commit 4213081d23

Verified by me against `gerrit/main`, not on a report. The change is
`4213081d23` *Split DC transport into capability mixins*, carrying
`rebar-ticket: 465d-c541-5e52-4e62`.

### The structural claims — proven from the commit, not asserted

**"No test assertion is edited" / "pass UNEDITED" (AC1, AC2, AC3):** the commit touches
**7 source files and 0 test files**. That is the strongest available form of this evidence — a
relocation that edits no test cannot have adjusted an oracle to fit. Confirmed by running the tier
on the landed tree: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` -> **2244 passed, 0 failed** (50s).

**AC4 — module sizes.** Split products: `_base.py` 157, `_hierarchy.py` 199, `_issues.py` 309,
`_links.py` 110, `_people.py` 177; `transport.py` reduced to 230, `backend.py` 441. All inside the
100-500 band, none near the 800 cap. (`__init__.py` is 28 LOC, but it is the package marker, not a
split product — the docstring it carries is AC6's deliverable.)

**AC5 — exactly ONE `_resolve_epic_link_field_id`:** `grep -rn 'def _resolve_epic_link_field_id' src/`
returns exactly 1 hit, `_hierarchy.py:30`. The duplication 9bb9 avoided was not reintroduced.

**AC6 — organising principle stated:** `__init__.py:16-25` states it explicitly — one module per
capability aligned to the `_backend.py` Protocols — names every module, and justifies `_links.py`
co-locating `SupportsLinks` + `SupportsComments` because each alone is under the module-size floor.
It also directs a new operation's home by *which capability it is*, not by which file has headroom,
which is precisely what the criterion asked for. (I nearly recorded this as NOT met from a truncated
14-line read; reading the whole file reversed it.)

**AC7 — landed before further parent work:** `4213081d23` is on main; the parent/hierarchy work
([rebar:9f26-66c2-14af-4223] / [rebar:4b9e-bcad-456a-4233]) is in flight AFTER it, and is being
authored against the post-split layout.

### A real consequence of this split, tracked rather than hidden

The relocation emptied `transport.py` of its `search_issues` call sites, and the DC pagination
structural guard AST-scans that file — so **the guard is now vacuous and passes unconditionally**
(measured: 0 call sites). That is the same defect class as bug 59b2's vacuous assertions. It is NOT
a reason to hold this ticket open — the relocation is complete and correct — but it is a real
regression in protection caused by it, filed as [rebar:34c2-...] via [rebar:18a4-...]. Recording it
here so the causal link is not lost.

`file_impact` was undeclared; I set it to the commit's actual 7 files.
